transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Elena Zhou (Redwood SE); Chris Dalton (Redwood Solutions); Maya Torres (Crestline); Derek Nguyen (Crestline); Priya Iyer (Crestline); Jason Kim (Crestline procurement)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a POC to validate tail latency and cost tradeoffs for Crestline's checkout recommendation microservice. Focus: characterize QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, replayable benchmark, and pass/fail success criteria. Decided to run a 2-hr replay on Redwood Dedicated nodes with sampled traffic and a canary open-model for fallback.

Topics:
- Workload shape (steady, promotions bursts, diurnal, weekend spikes)
- Token mix (short vs long prompts, templated user data, embeddings vs generation)
- Concurrency & QPS mapping to GPU counts
- Benchmarks: metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, error rate)
- Timeline and next steps

[00:00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Maya (Crestline): Maya here. Hi.
[00:00:09] Derek (Crestline): Derek on the call.
[00:00:11] Priya (Crestline): Priya.
[00:00:12] Jason (Crestline): Jason.
[00:00:14] Samir: Great—Elena, Chris from our side?
[00:00:18] Elena (Redwood SE): Yep Elena here, will drive the tech bits.
[00:00:21] Chris (Redwood Solutions): Chris here.

[00:00:30] Samir: Objective for today — scope what we need for a POC so you can validate latency SLOs and unit economics. We're particularly interested in the checkout recommendation path, correct?
[00:00:39] Maya: Correct. The recommender runs as a sync call in our cart flow, and we need p95 below 220ms under normal load, with acceptable degradation during promo spikes. Also cost target is roughly $X per 1M tokens — we'll put exact in follow up.

[00:01:05] Elena: Can you walk through current topology? QPS, average tokens in and out, and concurrency at the service level?
[00:01:12] Derek: Sure. Baseline QPS is about 180 qps for the recommender across global regions; peak during promotions goes up to ~1,600 qps sustained for 20-40 minutes, with short bursts up to 4k qps for 30-60 seconds. Average prompt size is 120 input tokens, outputs average 40 tokens. There's also a smaller batch of long-context requests — about 5% of traffic — with input ~800 tokens and output ~300.

[00:02:01] [00:02:15] Priya: One nuance — some requests include user cart metadata embedded, which inflates token counts; we can strip PII before sharing logs but that will still show distribution.

[00:02:31] Chris (Redwood Solutions): Helpful. For the POC we typically ask for a 48-hour sample so we can build a traffic heatmap: QPS over time, concurrency distribution, token-length CDF. We'll run replay in two phases: baseline at typical load, then promo spike replay.

[00:02:51] [00:03:10] Maya: Sounds good. We also want to test fallback strategies — e.g., route to smaller quantized model or use a cached response for frequently seen carts. How do you simulate cache hits?

[00:03:22] Elena: We have a replay harness that can inject KV cache warmups and control cache hit rate. Note: sometimes transcription or docs say 'KV cash' in earlier exports — that's a typo — it's KV cache. We'll set a nominal cache hit scenario at 30% and a cold-cache run for worst-case tail.

[00:03:45] [00:04:05] Derek: Quick question: do you run the POC on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated? For production we prefer Dedicated but ok to run initial bench on hosted.

[00:04:12] Samir: We recommend starting on Dedicated capacity so throughput and latency match the production footprint. We can run a quick sanity test on Hosted to validate config. Dedicated also lets us pin model variants and replicate your network path if you use VPC peering.

[00:04:35] [00:04:55] Maya: What metrics will you capture during replay? We're especially worried about tail p99 and p999 latency for the promo bursts.

[00:05:01] Elena: We'll capture per-request: model_latency (token generation time), end_to_end_latency (network + inference), tokens_in, tokens_out, GPU_utilization, batching efficiency, and queueing depth. For tail we'll report p50/p95/p99/p999 and the distribution over time. We'll also compute cost per 1M tokens and simulated monthly cost at current QPS profile.

[00:05:32] [00:05:58] Priya: We require audit logs and SSO integration for the Dedicated environment. Any compliance pitfalls?

[00:06:05] Chris: For Dedicated Private we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration. We'll share our security pack; SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts are available. For the POC we can provide redacted audit logs.

[00:06:30] [00:06:50] Jason (Procurement): On pricing — will the POC incur charges? What's the typical estimate for a 2-hr replay on Dedicated?

[00:06:58] Samir: We'll provide an estimate in the benchmark plan. Typically a 2-hr replay at your peak footprint maps to N GPU-hours and associated infra; we'll include options (lowest-cost quantized model vs high-throughput FP16).

[00:07:20] [00:07:40] Maya: Let's talk mapping QPS->GPU. Approx numbers?

[00:07:45] Elena: Ballpark: for your median request size (120 in / 40 out) and using a redwood-optimized open LLM 13B quantized, one A100-style instance can sustain ~250-350 effective qps with continuous batching and 80-90% batching efficiency. But bursts and long-context requests need headroom; we generally model concurrency and use autoscale buffers. For your peak 1.6k qps sustained we'd look at ~6-8 GPUs depending on model variant and desired latency p95 target.

[00:08:37] [00:08:58] Derek: That makes sense. For the 5% long requests (800/300 tokens) how much does that skew GPU needs?

[00:09:05] Elena: Long-context requests reduce throughput dramatically; they can be 5-10x more expensive per request. If you have consistent long tails, we either route them to a dedicated pool (long-context nodes) or use a quantized variant to reduce cost. For a mixed workload we'll model a two-pool configuration in the benchmark.

[00:09:38] [00:09:58] Samir: For success criteria — what's your pass/fail?

[00:10:02] Maya: Primary: p95 <= 220ms for normal load. During promo spike we can accept p95 <= 700ms and p99 <= 2.5s. Unit economics: cost per 1M tokens should not exceed our target — we'll confirm a numeric threshold by Tuesday. Quality regressions: no more than 1.5% drop in click-through for recommendations in A/B testing against current model.

[00:10:33] [00:10:55] Priya: Also need failover behavior — if Dedicated nodes are saturated, can Redwood automatically failover to a lower-capacity hosted pool and what would latency look like?

[00:11:02] Elena: Yes we can configure smart routing with fallback to a smaller quantized model or to Hosted pool with different SLOs. We'll include failover latency profiles in the report. Note that any data routing to Hosted may have data-residency implications — we'll flag that.

[00:11:25] [00:11:45] Derek: Regarding the replay harness — can it simulate real client-side delays and network jitter? We need to reproduce queueing effects at the edge.

[00:11:52] Chris: The harness can replay inter-arrival times and preserve original timestamps, or you can rescale them to compress time for stress testing. We can also inject network latency distributions to emulate regional variance.

[00:12:10] [00:12:35] Maya: We have feature flags that sometimes change prompt templates. How do we ensure the benchmark reflects current template mix?

[00:12:40] Elena: Best to include versioned request logs and a mapping of template IDs to frequency. We'll instrument the replay to sample from template distribution. If that's hard, send us a representative CSV of template counts.

[00:12:58] [00:13:20] Derek: On data privacy — can we mask user identifiers in the logs?

[00:13:25] Samir: Absolutely — anonymization is fine. We only need tokenized payloads and timing info. If any PII remains, we can sign an NDA or run the POC in your VPC with a private deployment.

[00:13:45] [00:14:05] Jason: Procurement note — we'll need a short SOW for the POC and terms for data deletion post POC.

[00:14:12] Samir: We'll attach an SOW template with the benchmark plan.

[00:14:20] [00:14:40] Elena: Next, let's define the benchmark plan phases. Phase 1: traffic ingestion and heatmap generation from your 48h sample. Phase 2: baseline replay (2 hrs at median scale) to validate config. Phase 3: promo spike replay and failover scenarios. Phase 4: report and recommendations (model variants, quantization, pooling).

[00:15:01] [00:15:25] Maya: Timeline expectations? If we provide logs by Mar 8, when can we run replay?

[00:15:30] Samir: If we get the sample by Mar 8, Redwood SEs can prep harness and run a first baseline by Mar 11-12, and schedule the promo replay the week of Mar 21 as discussed. We'll aim to deliver the final report Mar 25.

[00:15:50] [00:16:15] Priya: For the report, include recommended autoscale thresholds, batch size knobs, and quantization guidance so our infra team can implement.

[00:16:22] Elena: Yes, we'll produce concrete knob recommendations and a small ops playbook: GPU counts per region, reserve headroom for bursts, cache warmup sequences, and rollbacks.

[00:16:40] [00:17:05] Derek: A nit — when you say quantized model, are you recommending INT8 or 4-bit? Any accuracy estimates?

[00:17:12] Elena: We'll test both 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants. Historically 8-bit gives near-zero quality delta, 4-bit may have minor degradations depending on prompt type. We'll include quality checks against your evaluation set; if accuracy drop is >1.5% we'll flag it.

[00:17:35] [00:17:58] Maya: For A/B quality we need to run evaluation traffic as part of the POC — can Redwood compute CTR delta during the replay?

[00:18:04] Chris: We can annotate replayed requests with test IDs so you can compute client-side metrics. We also compute synthetic relevance scores if you provide an evaluation set.

[00:18:20] [00:18:42] Jason: Any blockers on legal? We need a short data processing addendum.

[00:18:50] Samir: We'll loop Legal in parallel and provide a DPA addendum. For the POC we typically include data retention and deletion timelines.

[00:19:05] [00:19:35] Priya: Can we get a short list of telemetry endpoints and the CSV schema so our telemetry ingestion team can map fields?

[00:19:40] Elena: Yes — we'll send a telemetry schema and an example JSON lines file.

[00:19:55] [00:20:20] Maya: Cool. Any thoughts on routing strategy for long-context requests? Dedicated long-pool or on-demand spin-up?

[00:20:28] Elena: For predictable long-context traffic we prefer a dedicated long-context pool to avoid tail-impacting short requests. If long requests are rare, on-demand spin-up with a small warm pool is viable. We'll model both.

[00:20:50] [00:21:15] Derek: What about batching strategies — do you do dynamic batching across sessions or strict per-session constraints?

[00:21:22] Chris: We use continuous batching with kernel optimizations that respect per-request latency budgets. For low-latency SLOs we limit batch windows, and for throughput we widen them. We'll include batching efficiency metrics in the report. Sometimes the transcript generator shows 'Red wood' or other splits — ignore that; it's our engine.

[00:21:50] [00:22:12] Maya: Any other items we should confirm before sharing logs?

[00:22:18] Samir: Please include: 48h of request timestamps, template IDs, tokens_in/tokens_out, any flags that affect templates, regional origin. Also note any maintenance windows in that period.

[00:22:34] [00:22:55] Priya: We'll anonymize user ids and remove PII. Derek will assemble the sample.

[00:23:05] [00:23:30] Maya: One more: can Redwood run an initial synthetic run that exercises 4k qps bursts for 60s to validate autoscale?

[00:23:36] Elena: Yes we can run a compressed stress test that simulates extreme bursts, but we recommend the real-replay for accuracy. Stress runs are useful to validate autoscale and safety limits.

[00:23:55] [00:24:20] Samir: Ok let's recap next steps quickly.
[00:24:25] Elena: Action items recapped — Samir will send benchmark plan and SOW; Elena will send replay harness docs and telemetry schema; Derek will share 48h anonymized sample; Maya to confirm numeric cost target; Chris to propose dates for the 2-hr replay window.

[00:24:50] [00:25:10] Jason: Procurement to expect SOW and DPA.

[00:25:15] Samir: Anything else?
[00:25:20] Maya: No, that's good. Appreciate the thoroughness.

[00:25:25] Samir: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and link the benchmark doc.

[00:55:30] (call ends — remaining Q&A handled offline)

Notes & Observations (auto):
- Traffic mix heavy on short prompts but long-context tail is non-trivial (5%) which materially increases GPU needs if colocated.
- Promo bursts dominate capacity planning — autoscale + buffering recommended.
- Two-pool architecture (short/long) likely most cost-efficient.
- Need to validate 4-bit quantization on your evaluation set before recommending to production.
